A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

bacterial microbiomes of A. texana ants and their gardens were highly similar and dominated by the same bacterial taxa, but that the microbiomes of the foundress queens and their fungal starter-cultures were more diverse, and contained a higher proportion of bacteria from the genus Mesoplasmas.

the A. texana foundress queen microbiome is composed of bacteria from the gut of the queen and bacteria in her fungal inocula, whereas the bacterial microbiome of the fungal inocula is dominated by bacteria that are also present in the foundress queen gut.

bacterial microbiomes from A. texana are dominated by Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter in all life stages and habitats, and that the bacterial genus Mesplasma, which is a potential symbiont, was present in high abundance only in the fungal inoculum.

microbiome studies provide new insights into symbiotic relationships between ants and their microbiomes.
microbiomes of the fungal inoculum and the host ants are closely related.

microbiomes from vertically and horizontally transmitted fungal inocula are similar in composition, suggesting that microbiome surveys of vertically transmitted inocula can provide insights into the functional roles of microbiomes in the symbiotic relationship of ants and their gardens.
